source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עֵשָׂ֣ו בָּ֔א וְעִמּ֕וֹ אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּ֣חַץ אֶת־הַיְלָדִ֗ים עַל־לֵאָה֙ וְעַל־רָחֵ֔ל וְעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֥י הַשְּׁפָחֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And lifted up Jacob his eyes and saw, and behold, Esau [was] coming, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children between Leah and between Rachel and between the two slave women.

en.L: And Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked, and there was Esau coming, and four hundred men with him. And he divided the children among Leah and Rachel and the two slave women.
en.B: When Jacob looked up, he saw Esau approaching with four hundred men. So he shared out the children among Leah, Rachel and the two female servants.
en.R: Then Jacob saw Esau in the distance, and four hundred men were coming with him. So Jacob split the children into groups. He put each group with its mother: Leah, Rachel, or one of the two female servants.

es.L: Y alzó Jacob los ojos y miró, y he aquí que Esaú venía, y cuatrocientos hombres con él. Y repartió a los niños entre Lea, Raquel y las dos esclavas.
es.B: Cuando Jacob alzó la vista, vio que Esaú se acercaba con cuatrocientos hombres. Así que repartió a los niños entre Lea, Raquel y las dos siervas.
es.R: Entonces Jacob vio a Esaú a lo lejos, y venían cuatrocientos hombres con él. Así que Jacob separó a los niños en grupos. Puso a cada grupo con su madre: Lea, Raquel o una de las dos siervas.

fr.L: Et Jacob leva les yeux et regarda, et voici, Ésaü venait, et quatre cents hommes avec lui. Et il répartit les enfants entre Léa, Rachel et les deux esclaves.
fr.B: Quand Jacob leva les yeux, il vit Ésaü qui arrivait avec quatre cents hommes. Il répartit donc les enfants entre Léa, Rachel et les deux servantes.
fr.R: Puis Jacob a vu Ésaü au loin, et quatre cents hommes venaient avec lui. Alors Jacob a séparé les enfants en groupes. Il a mis chaque groupe avec sa mère : Léa, Rachel, ou l’une des deux servantes.

sw.L: Yakobo aliinua macho yake, akatazama, na tazama, Esau alikuwa anakuja, na watu mia nne pamoja naye. Akawagawanya watoto kwa Lea, na kwa Raheli, na kwa wale wajakazi wawili.
sw.B: Yakobo alipoinua macho, alimwona Esau akija na watu mia nne. Kwa hiyo akawagawa watoto kati ya Lea, Raheli na wale watumishi wawili wa kike.
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo alimwona Esau kwa mbali, na watu mia nne walikuwa wakija pamoja naye. Kwa hiyo Yakobo akawagawa watoto katika makundi. Kila kundi akaliweka pamoja na mama yao: Lea, Raheli, au mmoja wa wale watumishi wawili wa kike.

decisions.choice: four hundred men: a force the size of a raiding army
decisions.reason: The messengers had already reported these men (32:7). Four hundred is the size of David's fighting band (1 Samuel 22:2; 25:13); Jacob has every reason to fear an attack.

decisions.choice: female servants
decisions.reason: "Female servants" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "slave women".

decisions.choice: He put each group with its mother
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that each mother kept her own children with her, as verse 2 shows.

decisions.choice: passé simple at L and B ("leva", "répartit"); passé composé at R ("a vu", "a séparé")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide has it: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative in French, used at Literal and Balanced; Readable uses the passé composé, the past tense of spoken and school French. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וַיָּ֧שֶׂם אֶת־הַשְּׁפָח֛וֹת וְאֶת־יַלְדֵיהֶ֖ן רִֽאשֹׁנָ֑ה וְאֶת־לֵאָ֤ה וִֽילָדֶ֨יהָ֙ אַחֲרֹנִ֔ים וְאֶת־רָחֵ֥ל וְאֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף אַחֲרֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put the slave women and their children first, and Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph last.

en.L: And he put the slave women and their children first, and Leah and her children after [them], and Rachel and Joseph last.
en.B: He placed the female servants with their children at the front, Leah with hers behind them, and Rachel with Joseph at the very back.
en.R: The female servants and their children went at the front. Behind them were Leah and her children. Rachel and Joseph were at the very back.

es.L: Y puso a las esclavas y a sus hijos primero, y a Lea y a sus hijos después [de ellas], y a Raquel y a José al final.
es.B: Colocó a las siervas con sus hijos al frente, a Lea con los suyos detrás de ellas, y a Raquel con José al final de todo.
es.R: Las siervas y sus hijos iban delante. Detrás de ellos estaban Lea y sus hijos. Raquel y José iban al final de todo.

fr.L: Et il plaça les esclaves et leurs enfants en premier, et Léa et ses enfants après [elles], et Rachel et Joseph en dernier.
fr.B: Il mit les servantes avec leurs enfants devant, Léa avec les siens derrière elles, et Rachel avec Joseph tout à l’arrière.
fr.R: Les servantes et leurs enfants marchaient devant. Derrière eux, il y avait Léa et ses enfants. Rachel et Joseph étaient tout à l’arrière.

sw.L: Akawaweka wajakazi na watoto wao mbele, na Lea na watoto wake nyuma [yao], na Raheli na Yusufu mwisho.
sw.B: Aliwaweka watumishi wa kike pamoja na watoto wao mbele, Lea na watoto wake nyuma yao, na Raheli pamoja na Yusufu nyuma kabisa.
sw.R: Watumishi wa kike na watoto wao walitangulia mbele. Nyuma yao walikuwa Lea na watoto wake. Raheli na Yusufu walikuwa nyuma kabisa.

decisions.choice: first ... after ... last: the most loved at the back, furthest from danger
decisions.reason: If Esau attacked, those at the front would meet him first. The order shows whom Jacob prized most, Rachel and her son Joseph, a favoritism that will shape the story of Joseph (37:3-4).

decisions.choice: female servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וְה֖וּא עָבַ֣ר לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֤חוּ אַ֨רְצָה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים עַד־גִּשְׁתּ֖וֹ עַד־אָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he passed on before them, and bowed down to [the] ground seven times until he drew near to his brother.

en.L: And he himself went on ahead of them and bowed down to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
en.B: Jacob himself went ahead of them all, and on his way toward his brother he bowed to the ground seven times.
en.R: Jacob walked ahead of everyone. As he came near his brother, he bowed down with his face to the ground seven times.

es.L: Y él mismo pasó delante de ellos, y se inclinó a tierra siete veces, hasta que llegó cerca de su hermano.
es.B: Jacob mismo se adelantó a todos, y mientras avanzaba hacia su hermano, se inclinó hasta el suelo siete veces.
es.R: Jacob caminó delante de todos. Al acercarse a su hermano, se inclinó siete veces con la cara hasta el suelo.

fr.L: Et lui-même passa devant eux, et il se prosterna jusqu’à terre sept fois, jusqu’à ce qu’il arrive près de son frère.
fr.B: Jacob lui-même passa en tête de tous, et en s’avançant vers son frère, il se prosterna sept fois jusqu’à terre.
fr.R: Jacob a marché devant tout le monde. En arrivant près de son frère, il s’est incliné sept fois, le visage contre terre.

sw.L: Naye mwenyewe akapita mbele yao, akasujudu mpaka chini mara saba, hata alipomkaribia ndugu yake.
sw.B: Yakobo mwenyewe aliwatangulia wote, na alipokuwa akimwendea ndugu yake, akainama mpaka chini mara saba.
sw.R: Yakobo alitembea mbele ya wote. Alipomkaribia ndugu yake, aliinama mara saba, uso wake ukigusa ardhi.

decisions.choice: bowed down seven times: the bow of a subject before his ruler
decisions.reason: Letters written to Egypt's king in the fourteenth century BC open with the words that the writer falls at the king's feet "seven times and seven times". Jacob comes to Esau as a servant to his lord, the reverse of the blessing he had taken: "may your mother's sons bow down to you" (27:29).

decisions.choice: he himself went on ahead: Jacob puts himself in front
decisions.reason: In 32:17-21 Jacob sent everything ahead of himself. Now, after the night at Peniel, he goes first and meets Esau face to face.

source.text: וַיָּ֨רָץ עֵשָׂ֤ו לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַֽיְחַבְּקֵ֔הוּ וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל־צַוָּארָ֖ווַׄיִּׄשָּׁׄקֵ֑ׄהׄוּׄוַיִּבְכּֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And ran Esau to meet him and embraced him and fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept.

en.L: And Esau ran to meet him and embraced him and fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept.
en.B: But Esau ran to meet him and hugged him; he held him close and kissed him, and they wept together.
en.R: But Esau ran to meet Jacob. He hugged him tight and kissed him, and the two brothers cried together.

es.L: Y Esaú corrió a su encuentro, lo abrazó, se echó sobre su cuello y lo besó, y lloraron.
es.B: Pero Esaú corrió a su encuentro y lo abrazó; lo estrechó contra sí y lo besó, y lloraron juntos.
es.R: Pero Esaú corrió hacia Jacob. Lo abrazó fuerte y lo besó, y los dos hermanos lloraron juntos.

fr.L: Et Ésaü courut à sa rencontre, l’étreignit, tomba à son cou et l’embrassa, et ils pleurèrent.
fr.B: Mais Ésaü courut à sa rencontre et le serra dans ses bras ; il le tint contre lui et l’embrassa, et ils pleurèrent ensemble.
fr.R: Mais Ésaü a couru vers Jacob. Il l’a serré très fort dans ses bras et l’a embrassé, et les deux frères ont pleuré ensemble.

sw.L: Esau akapiga mbio kumlaki, akamkumbatia, akaangukia shingo yake, akambusu, wakalia.
sw.B: Lakini Esau alikimbia kumlaki, akamkumbatia; akamshika kifuani na kumbusu, nao wakalia pamoja.
sw.R: Lakini Esau alikimbia kumlaki Yakobo. Akamkumbatia kwa nguvu na kumbusu, na ndugu hao wawili wakalia pamoja.

decisions.choice: ran ... embraced ... fell on his neck ... kissed: a welcome instead of revenge
decisions.reason: Jacob feared Esau would kill him (27:41; 32:11). Instead Esau runs to him. The same picture returns when Joseph meets Benjamin and Jacob (45:14; 46:29), and in Jesus' parable of the father who runs to his returning son (Luke 15:20).

decisions.choice: and kissed him, as written; the scribes marked the word with dots
decisions.reason: In the Masoretic text the word "and kissed him" carries a row of dots above its letters, one of a small number of words so marked. The purpose of the marking is not known; later Jewish teachers debated whether it questions the sincerity of the kiss. The words themselves are not in doubt.

decisions.choice: fell on his neck (L); held him close (B); hugged him tight (R)
decisions.reason: To fall on someone's neck is to throw one's arms around him in a close embrace. Literal keeps the idiom; Balanced and Readable give its sense.

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א אֶת־עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֤רְא אֶת־הַנָּשִׁים֙ וְאֶת־הַיְלָדִ֔ים וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּאמַ֕ר הַיְלָדִ֕ים אֲשֶׁר־חָנַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children and said, who [are] these with you? And he said, the children whom has graciously given God your servant.

en.L: And he lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, "Who [are] these with you?" And he said, "The children whom God has graciously given your servant."
en.B: Esau looked up, and when he saw the women and children he asked, "Who are all these with you?" "They are the children God has favored your servant with," Jacob said.
en.R: When Esau saw the women and children, he asked, "Who are all these people with you?" Jacob said, "They are the children God was kind enough to give me, your servant."

es.L: Y alzó los ojos y vio a las mujeres y a los niños, y dijo: «¿Quiénes [son] estos contigo?». Y él dijo: «Los niños que Dios ha concedido por su gracia a tu siervo».
es.B: Esaú alzó la vista y, al ver a las mujeres y a los niños, preguntó: «¿Quiénes son todos estos que vienen contigo?». «Son los hijos con que Dios ha favorecido a tu siervo», respondió Jacob.
es.R: Cuando Esaú vio a las mujeres y a los niños, preguntó: «¿Quiénes son todas estas personas que vienen contigo?». Jacob dijo: «Son los hijos que Dios, en su bondad, me ha dado a mí, tu siervo».

fr.L: Et il leva les yeux et vit les femmes et les enfants, et dit : « Qui [sont] ceux-ci avec toi ? » Et il dit : « Les enfants que Dieu a accordés par grâce à ton serviteur. »
fr.B: Ésaü leva les yeux, et en voyant les femmes et les enfants, il demanda : « Qui sont tous ceux-là, avec toi ? » « Ce sont les enfants dont Dieu a fait la faveur à ton serviteur », répondit Jacob.
fr.R: Quand Ésaü a vu les femmes et les enfants, il a demandé : « Qui sont tous ces gens avec toi ? » Jacob a répondu : « Ce sont les enfants que Dieu, dans sa bonté, m’a donnés, à moi, ton serviteur. »

sw.L: Akainua macho yake, akawaona wale wanawake na watoto, akasema, "Hawa walio pamoja nawe [ni] nani?" Akasema, "Ni watoto ambao Mungu amemjalia mtumishi wako kwa neema."
sw.B: Esau alipoinua macho na kuwaona wanawake na watoto, aliuliza, "Hawa wote walio pamoja nawe ni nani?" Yakobo akasema, "Ni watoto ambao Mungu amemfadhili nao mtumishi wako."
sw.R: Esau alipowaona wanawake na watoto, aliuliza, "Watu hawa wote walio pamoja nawe ni akina nani?" Yakobo akasema, "Ni watoto ambao Mungu kwa wema wake amenipa mimi, mtumishi wako."

decisions.choice: graciously given: favor freely shown
decisions.reason: The verb chanan (to be gracious) shares its root with chen, "favor", which Jacob asks for again and again in this meeting (verses 8, 10, 15). He credits his family to God's undeserved kindness, and asks the same kindness of his brother.

decisions.choice: your servant: Jacob speaks of himself as Esau's servant
decisions.reason: Calling oneself "your servant" and the other "my lord" was the polite speech of an inferior to a superior. Jacob keeps it up through the whole meeting (32:5; 33:8, 13-15), while Esau calls him "my brother" (verse 9).

decisions.choice: me, your servant
decisions.reason: Readable adds "me" so that a reader sees Jacob is speaking of himself.

source.text: וַתִּגַּ֧שְׁןָ הַשְּׁפָח֛וֹת הֵ֥נָּה וְיַלְדֵיהֶ֖ן וַתִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶֽיןָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And approached the slave women, they and their children, and they bowed down.

en.L: And the slave women came near, they and their children, and they bowed down.
en.B: Then the female servants came forward with their children and bowed low.
en.R: Then the female servants and their children came up to Esau and bowed down.

es.L: Y se acercaron las esclavas, ellas y sus hijos, y se inclinaron.
es.B: Luego las siervas se adelantaron con sus hijos y se inclinaron profundamente.
es.R: Después, las siervas y sus hijos se acercaron a Esaú y se inclinaron.

fr.L: Et les esclaves s’approchèrent, elles et leurs enfants, et ils se prosternèrent.
fr.B: Puis les servantes s’avancèrent avec leurs enfants et s’inclinèrent profondément.
fr.R: Ensuite, les servantes et leurs enfants se sont approchés d’Ésaü et se sont inclinés.

sw.L: Wale wajakazi wakakaribia, wao na watoto wao, wakasujudu.
sw.B: Kisha watumishi wa kike walisogea mbele pamoja na watoto wao, wakainama sana.
sw.R: Kisha watumishi wa kike na watoto wao walimwendea Esau, wakainama.

decisions.choice: female servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַתִּגַּ֧שׁ גַּם־לֵאָ֛ה וִילָדֶ֖יהָ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֑וּ וְאַחַ֗ר נִגַּ֥שׁ יוֹסֵ֛ף וְרָחֵ֖ל וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And approached also Leah and her children, and they bowed down; and after, approached Joseph and Rachel, and they bowed down.

en.L: And Leah also came near with her children, and they bowed down; and afterward Joseph and Rachel came near, and they bowed down.
en.B: Leah and her children came forward next and bowed, and last of all Joseph and Rachel came forward and bowed.
en.R: After them came Leah and her children, and they bowed down too. Then Joseph and Rachel came forward and bowed down.

es.L: Y se acercó también Lea con sus hijos, y se inclinaron; y después se acercaron José y Raquel, y se inclinaron.
es.B: Lea y sus hijos se adelantaron después y se inclinaron, y por último se adelantaron José y Raquel y se inclinaron.
es.R: Después de ellos vinieron Lea y sus hijos, y también se inclinaron. Luego José y Raquel se acercaron y se inclinaron.

fr.L: Et Léa aussi s’approcha avec ses enfants, et ils se prosternèrent ; et ensuite Joseph et Rachel s’approchèrent, et ils se prosternèrent.
fr.B: Léa et ses enfants s’avancèrent à leur tour et s’inclinèrent, et en dernier, Joseph et Rachel s’avancèrent et s’inclinèrent.
fr.R: Après eux sont venus Léa et ses enfants, et ils se sont inclinés, eux aussi. Puis Joseph et Rachel se sont avancés et se sont inclinés.

sw.L: Lea naye akakaribia pamoja na watoto wake, wakasujudu; kisha Yusufu na Raheli wakakaribia, wakasujudu.
sw.B: Lea na watoto wake walisogea mbele baadaye, wakainama; na mwisho kabisa Yusufu na Raheli wakasogea mbele, wakainama.
sw.R: Baada yao wakaja Lea na watoto wake, nao wakainama pia. Kisha Yusufu na Raheli wakaja mbele, wakainama.

decisions.choice: Joseph and Rachel: the son named before his mother
decisions.reason: With the other groups the mother is named first. Here Joseph comes first, perhaps because he stepped forward in front of his mother; the story is already turning toward him.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י לְךָ֛ כָּל־הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּגָ֑שְׁתִּי וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לִמְצֹא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, who [is] to you all this camp which I met? And he said, to find favor in [the] eyes of my lord.

en.L: And he said, "What [is] all this camp of yours that I met?" And he said, "To find favor in the eyes of my lord."
en.B: "And what were all those herds I ran into?" Esau asked. "They were meant to win my lord's goodwill," Jacob replied.
en.R: Esau asked, "Why did you send all those groups of animals that I met?" Jacob answered, "I wanted you to be kind to me, my lord."

es.L: Y dijo: «¿Qué [es] para ti todo este campamento que he encontrado?». Y él dijo: «Para hallar gracia ante los ojos de mi señor».
es.B: «¿Y qué eran todos esos rebaños con los que me he cruzado?», preguntó Esaú. «Eran para ganarme el favor de mi señor», respondió Jacob.
es.R: Esaú preguntó: «¿Por qué me mandaste todos esos grupos de animales que encontré?». Jacob respondió: «Quería que fueras bueno conmigo, mi señor».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Que [signifie] pour toi tout ce camp que j’ai rencontré ? » Et il dit : « Pour trouver grâce aux yeux de mon seigneur. »
fr.B: « Et que voulaient dire tous ces troupeaux que j’ai croisés ? » demanda Ésaü. « Ils devaient me gagner la bienveillance de mon seigneur », répondit Jacob.
fr.R: Ésaü a demandé : « Pourquoi m’as-tu envoyé tous ces groupes d’animaux que j’ai rencontrés ? » Jacob a répondu : « Je voulais que tu sois bon pour moi, mon seigneur. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Kambi hii yote niliyokutana nayo [ni] ya nini kwako?" Akasema, "Ili nipate kibali machoni pa bwana wangu."
sw.B: "Na yale makundi yote niliyokutana nayo njiani ni ya nini?" Esau akauliza. "Yalikuwa ya kunipatia fadhili za bwana wangu," Yakobo akajibu.
sw.R: Esau akauliza, "Kwa nini ulituma makundi yale yote ya wanyama niliyokutana nayo?" Yakobo akajibu, "Nilitaka unitendee wema, bwana wangu."

decisions.choice: all this camp: the droves of animals sent ahead as a gift
decisions.reason: Jacob had sent over five hundred animals in separate droves, each with a message (32:14-21). The word for camp (machaneh) is the one behind Mahanaim, "two camps" (32:2-3, 8).

decisions.choice: to find favor in the eyes of my lord: to win your goodwill
decisions.reason: To find favor in someone's eyes is to be looked on kindly by him. Jacob uses the phrase three times in this meeting (verses 8, 10, 15).

decisions.choice: all those herds (B); all those groups of animals (R)
decisions.reason: "Camp" would puzzle a reader; Balanced and Readable say what Esau met on the road.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר עֵשָׂ֖ו יֶשׁ־לִ֣י רָ֑ב אָחִ֕י יְהִ֥י לְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Esau, there is to me plenty, my brother; let be to you what [is] to you.

en.L: And Esau said, "I have plenty, my brother; let what [is] yours be yours."
en.B: "I have a great deal, my brother," said Esau. "Let what is yours stay yours."
en.R: Esau said, "My brother, I have a lot already. What is yours should stay yours."

es.L: Y dijo Esaú: «Tengo mucho, hermano mío; sea tuyo lo que [es] tuyo».
es.B: «Tengo de sobra, hermano mío», dijo Esaú. «Quédate con lo que es tuyo».
es.R: Esaú dijo: «Hermano, yo ya tengo mucho. Lo que es tuyo debe seguir siendo tuyo».

fr.L: Et Ésaü dit : « J’ai en abondance, mon frère ; que ce qui [est] à toi soit à toi. »
fr.B: « J’ai beaucoup de biens, mon frère, dit Ésaü. Garde ce qui est à toi. »
fr.R: Ésaü a dit : « Mon frère, j’ai déjà beaucoup. Ce qui est à toi doit rester à toi. »

sw.L: Esau akasema, "Nina vingi, ndugu yangu; kilicho chako kiwe chako."
sw.B: "Nina mali nyingi, ndugu yangu," Esau akasema. "Kilicho chako kibaki kuwa chako."
sw.R: Esau akasema, "Ndugu yangu, tayari nina vitu vingi. Vilivyo vyako na vibaki kuwa vyako."

decisions.choice: I have plenty: Esau answers "plenty", Jacob will answer "everything"
decisions.reason: Esau says he has "much" (rav); Jacob replies that he has "everything" (verse 11). Esau also calls Jacob "my brother" while Jacob keeps calling Esau "my lord".

decisions.choice: plenty: rav, the word of the old oracle
decisions.reason: Before the twins were born, God said that "the older (rav) will serve the younger" (25:23). The same word now describes the older brother's wealth.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֗ב אַל־נָא֙ אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ מִנְחָתִ֖י מִיָּדִ֑י כִּ֣י עַל־כֵּ֞ן רָאִ֣יתִי פָנֶ֗יךָ כִּרְאֹ֛ת פְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַתִּרְצֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jacob, no, please; if, please, I have found favor in your eyes, then take my gift from my hand; for therefore I have seen your face like seeing [the] face of God, and you have received me favorably.

en.L: And Jacob said, "No, please; if I have found favor in your eyes, then take my gift from my hand, for indeed I have seen your face as one sees the face of God, and you have received me favorably.
en.B: "Please, no," Jacob said. "If you look on me with favor, take my gift from my hand. Looking on your face has been like looking on the face of God, so graciously have you received me.
en.R: Jacob said, "No, please! If you are pleased with me, then accept my gift. Seeing your kind face is like seeing the face of God, because you have welcomed me.

es.L: Y dijo Jacob: «No, te ruego; si he hallado gracia ante tus ojos, toma mi presente de mi mano, porque ciertamente he visto tu rostro como quien ve el rostro de Dios, y me has recibido con agrado.
es.B: «Por favor, no», dijo Jacob. «Si me miras con favor, acepta de mi mano mi regalo. Ver tu rostro ha sido como ver el rostro de Dios, con tanta bondad me has recibido.
es.R: Jacob dijo: «¡No, por favor! Si estás contento conmigo, acepta mi regalo. Ver tu cara bondadosa es como ver la cara de Dios, porque me has recibido bien.

fr.L: Et Jacob dit : « Non, je te prie ; si j’ai trouvé grâce à tes yeux, prends donc mon présent de ma main, car en vérité j’ai vu ta face comme on voit la face de Dieu, et tu m’as accueilli favorablement.
fr.B: « Non, je t’en prie, dit Jacob. Si tu me regardes avec bienveillance, accepte de ma main mon présent. Voir ton visage a été pour moi comme voir le visage de Dieu, tant tu m’as reçu avec bonté.
fr.R: Jacob a dit : « Non, s’il te plaît ! Si tu es content de moi, accepte mon cadeau. Voir ton visage plein de bonté, c’est comme voir le visage de Dieu, parce que tu m’as bien accueilli.

sw.L: Yakobo akasema, "Sivyo, nakuomba; ikiwa nimepata kibali machoni pako, basi pokea zawadi yangu kutoka mkononi mwangu, kwa maana hakika nimeuona uso wako kama mtu auonavyo uso wa Mungu, nawe umenipokea kwa radhi.
sw.B: "Hapana, tafadhali," Yakobo akasema. "Ikiwa unanitazama kwa fadhili, pokea zawadi yangu kutoka mkononi mwangu. Kuuona uso wako kumekuwa kama kuuona uso wa Mungu, kwa jinsi ulivyonipokea kwa wema.
sw.R: Yakobo akasema, "Hapana, tafadhali! Kama umependezwa nami, pokea zawadi yangu. Kuuona uso wako wenye upole ni kama kuuona uso wa Mungu, kwa sababu umenikaribisha vizuri.

decisions.choice: seen your face as one sees the face of God: an echo of Peniel
decisions.reason: The night before, Jacob wrestled and named the place Peniel, "face of God", saying "I have seen God face to face" (32:31). Before that he had hoped the gift would cover Esau's face so he could see his face (32:21). He now finds in his brother's welcome the same grace he met there.

decisions.choice: received me favorably: accepted me, as an offering is accepted
decisions.reason: The verb ratsah is often used of God accepting a sacrifice (Leviticus 1:4). Esau's acceptance of the gift means acceptance of Jacob himself.

decisions.choice: your kind face
decisions.reason: Readable adds "kind" to show what made Esau's face like God's face: his welcome, stated at the end of the verse.

source.text: קַח־נָ֤א אֶת־בִּרְכָתִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֻבָ֣את לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־חַנַּ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְכִ֣י יֶשׁ־לִי־כֹ֑ל וַיִּפְצַר־בּ֖וֹ וַיִּקָּֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: Take, please, my blessing which has been brought to you, for God has dealt graciously with me, and for there is to me everything. And he urged him, and he took [it].

en.L: Please take my blessing that has been brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have everything." And he urged him, and he took [it].
en.B: So take, I beg you, the blessing that was brought to you. God has been good to me, and I lack nothing." Jacob would not take no for an answer, and Esau accepted it.
en.R: Please take the gift I brought you. God has been very kind to me. I have everything." Jacob kept begging, so in the end Esau took it.

es.L: Toma, te ruego, mi bendición que te ha sido traída, porque Dios me ha favorecido, y porque yo tengo de todo». E insistió con él, y él [la] tomó.
es.B: Acepta, te lo suplico, la bendición que te han traído. Dios ha sido bueno conmigo, y no me falta nada». Jacob insistió tanto que Esaú la aceptó.
es.R: Por favor, toma el regalo que te traje. Dios ha sido muy bueno conmigo. Lo tengo todo». Jacob siguió rogándole, y al fin Esaú lo tomó.

fr.L: Prends, je te prie, ma bénédiction qui t’a été apportée, car Dieu m’a fait grâce, et parce que j’ai tout. » Et il insista auprès de lui, et il [la] prit.
fr.B: Accepte donc, je t’en supplie, la bénédiction qu’on t’a apportée. Dieu a été bon pour moi, et je ne manque de rien. » Jacob insista tant qu’Ésaü accepta.
fr.R: S’il te plaît, prends le cadeau que je t’ai apporté. Dieu a été très bon pour moi. J’ai tout ce qu’il me faut. » Jacob a continué à insister, et finalement Ésaü l’a pris.

sw.L: Tafadhali pokea baraka yangu iliyoletwa kwako, kwa kuwa Mungu amenitendea kwa neema, na kwa kuwa nina kila kitu." Akamsihi sana, naye akaipokea.
sw.B: Basi pokea, nakusihi, baraka uliyoletewa. Mungu amekuwa mwema kwangu, wala sipungukiwi na kitu." Yakobo akaendelea kumsihi, hata Esau akaikubali.
sw.R: Tafadhali pokea zawadi niliyokuletea. Mungu amekuwa mwema sana kwangu. Nina kila kitu." Yakobo akaendelea kumsihi, hatimaye Esau akaipokea.

decisions.choice: my blessing: here, a gift, but also the word of the stolen blessing
decisions.reason: Berakhah can mean a gift that comes with good wishes (1 Samuel 25:27). It is also the word for the blessing Jacob took from Esau by deceit (27:35-36). Giving his "blessing" to Esau may be Jacob's way of paying back what he once took.

decisions.choice: I have everything: more than Esau's "plenty"
decisions.reason: Jacob answers Esau's "I have plenty" (verse 9) with "I have everything", because God has been gracious to him.

decisions.choice: this gift
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain sense; Literal and Balanced keep "blessing" so that the link with chapter 27 can be seen.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר נִסְעָ֣ה וְנֵלֵ֑כָה וְאֵלְכָ֖ה לְנֶגְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, let us set out and let us go, and I will go before you.

en.L: And he said, "Let us set out and go, and I will go alongside you."
en.B: Esau said, "Come, let us break camp and move on. I will go alongside you."
en.R: Then Esau said, "Let us get going. I will travel with you."

es.L: Y dijo: «Partamos y vayamos, y yo iré junto a ti».
es.B: Esaú dijo: «Vamos, levantemos el campamento y sigamos adelante. Yo iré a tu lado».
es.R: Luego Esaú dijo: «Pongámonos en marcha. Yo viajaré contigo».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Partons et allons, et j’irai à côté de toi. »
fr.B: Ésaü dit : « Allons, levons le camp et mettons-nous en route. Je marcherai à tes côtés. »
fr.R: Puis Ésaü a dit : « Allons-y. Je vais voyager avec toi. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Na tuondoke twende, nami nitakwenda sambamba nawe."
sw.B: Esau akasema, "Haya, tuvunje kambi tuendelee na safari. Nitatembea kando yako."
sw.R: Kisha Esau akasema, "Tuondoke sasa. Nitasafiri pamoja nawe."

decisions.choice: I will go alongside you: travel with you, perhaps as an escort
alternatives: I will go ahead of you
decisions.reason: Lenegdekha usually means "opposite" or "in front of" you. Here it may mean Esau will lead the way, or that he will travel beside Jacob and his company.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֲדֹנִ֤י יֹדֵ֨עַ֙ כִּֽי־הַיְלָדִ֣ים רַכִּ֔ים וְהַצֹּ֥אן וְהַבָּקָ֖ר עָל֣וֹת עָלָ֑י וּדְפָקוּם֙ י֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד וָמֵ֖תוּ כָּל־הַצֹּֽאן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, my lord knows that the children [are] tender, and the flocks and the herds nursing [are] on me; and if they drive them hard one day, then will die all the flocks.

en.L: And he said to him, "My lord knows that the children [are] frail, and that the flocks and herds that are nursing [are] in my care; and if they are driven hard for one day, all the flocks will die.
en.B: But Jacob said to him, "As my lord can see, the children are small, and I have to look after sheep, goats and cattle that are suckling their young. If they are pushed too hard for even a single day, the whole flock will die.
en.R: But Jacob answered, "My lord, you know that the children are young and weak. And I must take care of the sheep, goats and cattle that are feeding their young. If they are pushed hard for even one day, the animals will all die.

es.L: Y le dijo: «Mi señor sabe que los niños [son] tiernos, y que las ovejas y las vacas que crían [están] a mi cargo; y si las fatigan un solo día, morirá todo el rebaño.
es.B: Pero Jacob le respondió: «Como mi señor puede ver, los niños son pequeños, y tengo que cuidar ovejas, cabras y vacas que están criando. Si se las apura demasiado, aunque sea un solo día, morirá todo el rebaño.
es.R: Pero Jacob le contestó: «Mi señor, tú sabes que los niños son pequeños y débiles. Además, tengo que cuidar las ovejas, las cabras y las vacas que están dando de mamar a sus crías. Si las hacemos caminar muy rápido, aunque sea un día, se morirán todos los animales.

fr.L: Et il lui dit : « Mon seigneur sait que les enfants [sont] fragiles, et que les brebis et les vaches qui allaitent [sont] à ma charge ; si on les presse un seul jour, tout le troupeau mourra.
fr.B: Mais Jacob lui répondit : « Mon seigneur le voit, les enfants sont petits, et je dois prendre soin des brebis, des chèvres et des vaches qui allaitent leurs petits. Si on les force à avancer trop vite, ne serait-ce qu’un seul jour, tout le troupeau mourra.
fr.R: Mais Jacob a répondu : « Mon seigneur, tu sais que les enfants sont jeunes et faibles. Et je dois m’occuper des moutons, des chèvres et des vaches qui nourrissent leurs petits. Si on les fait marcher trop vite, même un seul jour, toutes les bêtes vont mourir.

sw.L: Akamwambia, "Bwana wangu anajua kwamba watoto [ni] wachanga, na kwamba kondoo na ng'ombe wanaonyonyesha [wako] chini ya uangalizi wangu; wakiendeshwa kwa nguvu siku moja tu, kundi lote litakufa.
sw.B: Lakini Yakobo akamwambia, "Kama bwana wangu aonavyo, watoto ni wadogo, nami ninapaswa kuwatunza kondoo, mbuzi na ng'ombe wanaonyonyesha watoto wao. Wakiharakishwa kupita kiasi hata kwa siku moja tu, kundi zima litakufa.
sw.R: Lakini Yakobo akajibu, "Bwana wangu, unajua kwamba watoto ni wadogo na dhaifu. Tena ninapaswa kuwatunza kondoo, mbuzi na ng'ombe wanaonyonyesha watoto wao. Wakiendeshwa kwa haraka hata siku moja tu, wanyama wote watakufa.

decisions.choice: nursing: ewes and cows with young
decisions.reason: Animals with suckling young must move slowly and graze as they go; a hard march would cost them their milk and their young.

decisions.choice: they are driven hard
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "they drive them" with no named subject, a common way to say "someone drives them"; Literal uses the passive.

source.text: יַעֲבָר־נָ֥א אֲדֹנִ֖י לִפְנֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַאֲנִ֞י אֶֽתְנָהֲלָ֣הלְאִטִּ֗י לְרֶ֨גֶל הַמְּלָאכָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־לְפָנַי֙ וּלְרֶ֣גֶל הַיְלָדִ֔ים עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־אָבֹ֥א אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֖י שֵׂעִֽירָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Let pass on, please, my lord before his servant, and I will journey on at my slowness, at [the] pace of the property which [is] before me and at [the] pace of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir.

en.L: Please let my lord pass on ahead of his servant, and I will lead on gently, at the pace of the livestock that [are] before me and at the pace of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir."
en.B: Please, my lord, go on ahead of your servant. I will follow slowly, as fast as the animals in front of me and the children can go, until I reach my lord in Seir."
en.R: Please, my lord, go on ahead of me. I will come along slowly, as fast as my animals and the children can walk. Then I will meet you in Seir."

es.L: Pase, te ruego, mi señor delante de su siervo, y yo avanzaré despacio, al paso del ganado que [va] delante de mí y al paso de los niños, hasta que llegue a mi señor en Seír».
es.B: Por favor, mi señor, adelántate a tu siervo. Yo te seguiré despacio, al ritmo que puedan llevar los animales que van delante de mí y los niños, hasta reunirme con mi señor en Seír».
es.R: Por favor, mi señor, ve tú delante de mí. Yo iré despacio, tan rápido como puedan caminar mis animales y los niños. Luego me encontraré contigo en Seír».

fr.L: Que mon seigneur passe donc devant son serviteur, et moi, je m’avancerai doucement, au pas du bétail qui [est] devant moi et au pas des enfants, jusqu’à ce que j’arrive chez mon seigneur, à Séir. »
fr.B: Je t’en prie, mon seigneur, pars en avant de ton serviteur. Moi, je suivrai lentement, aussi vite que peuvent aller les bêtes qui sont devant moi et les enfants, jusqu’à ce que je rejoigne mon seigneur à Séir. »
fr.R: S’il te plaît, mon seigneur, pars devant moi. Je viendrai lentement, aussi vite que mes bêtes et les enfants peuvent marcher. Ensuite, je te retrouverai à Séir. »

sw.L: Tafadhali bwana wangu na apite mbele ya mtumishi wake, nami nitaendelea taratibu, kwa mwendo wa mifugo iliyo mbele yangu na kwa mwendo wa watoto, mpaka nitakapomfikia bwana wangu huko Seiri."
sw.B: Tafadhali, bwana wangu, umtangulie mtumishi wako. Mimi nitafuata polepole, kwa kadiri wanyama walio mbele yangu na watoto wanavyoweza kwenda, mpaka nitakapomfikia bwana wangu huko Seiri."
sw.R: Tafadhali, bwana wangu, nitangulie. Mimi nitakuja polepole, kwa mwendo ambao wanyama wangu na watoto wanaweza kutembea. Kisha nitakukuta huko Seiri."

decisions.choice: until I come to my lord at Seir: a promise the story never shows kept
decisions.reason: Seir, Esau's country, lay to the south-east. Jacob turns west instead, to Succoth and Shechem (verses 17-18). Whether he meant to come later or was politely avoiding Esau, the text does not say; the brothers meet again at their father's burial (35:29).

decisions.choice: the pace of the livestock: literally, the foot of the work
decisions.reason: Melakhah usually means work; here it means property, the herds and flocks that are Jacob's livelihood. "At the foot of" means at their walking pace.

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Readable says "me" for Jacob's polite "his servant", which it has already explained in verse 5.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר עֵשָׂ֔ו אַצִּֽיגָה־נָּ֣א עִמְּךָ֔ מִן־הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתִּ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לָ֣מָּה זֶּ֔ה אֶמְצָא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Esau, let me leave, please, with you some of the people who [are] with me. And he said, why this? Let me find favor in [the] eyes of my lord.

en.L: And Esau said, "Let me leave with you some of the people who [are] with me." And he said, "Why this? Let me find favor in the eyes of my lord."
en.B: Esau said, "At least let me leave some of the people who are with me to go with you." "What need is there for that?" Jacob replied. "Only let me keep my lord's goodwill."
en.R: Esau said, "Then some of my men can stay with you." But Jacob answered, "There is no need for that. I only want you to be pleased with me, my lord."

es.L: Y dijo Esaú: «Permíteme dejar contigo algo de la gente que [está] conmigo». Y él dijo: «¿Para qué esto? Halle yo gracia ante los ojos de mi señor».
es.B: Esaú dijo: «Deja al menos que algunos de los hombres que vienen conmigo se queden para acompañarte». «¿Qué necesidad hay?», respondió Jacob. «Solo quiero conservar el favor de mi señor».
es.R: Esaú dijo: «Entonces algunos de mis hombres se quedarán contigo». Pero Jacob respondió: «No hace falta. Solo quiero que estés contento conmigo, mi señor».

fr.L: Et Ésaü dit : « Laisse-moi donc placer près de toi quelques-uns des gens qui [sont] avec moi. » Et il dit : « Pourquoi cela ? Que je trouve grâce aux yeux de mon seigneur ! »
fr.B: Ésaü dit : « Laisse-moi au moins te confier quelques-uns des hommes qui sont avec moi. » « À quoi bon ? répondit Jacob. Que je garde seulement la bienveillance de mon seigneur ! »
fr.R: Ésaü a dit : « Alors, quelques-uns de mes hommes vont rester avec toi. » Mais Jacob a répondu : « Ce n’est pas nécessaire. Je veux seulement que tu sois content de moi, mon seigneur. »

sw.L: Esau akasema, "Na niache kwako baadhi ya watu walio pamoja nami." Akasema, "Kwa nini hivyo? Nipate tu kibali machoni pa bwana wangu."
sw.B: Esau akasema, "Angalau niache baadhi ya watu walio pamoja nami waende nawe." "Kuna haja gani ya hivyo?" Yakobo akajibu. "Nipate tu fadhili za bwana wangu."
sw.R: Esau akasema, "Basi baadhi ya watu wangu watabaki nawe." Lakini Yakobo akajibu, "Hakuna haja. Ninataka tu upendezwe nami, bwana wangu."

decisions.choice: why this? let me find favor: there is no need; your goodwill is enough
decisions.reason: Jacob politely declines the escort. "Let me find favor in your eyes" here works almost like "thank you, but no".

source.text: וַיָּשָׁב֩ בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֥וּא עֵשָׂ֛ו לְדַרְכּ֖וֹ שֵׂעִֽירָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned on that day Esau on his way to Seir.

en.L: And Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
en.B: That day Esau turned back and took the road to Seir.
en.R: Esau left that same day and went back to Seir.

es.L: Y Esaú volvió aquel día por su camino a Seír.
es.B: Aquel día Esaú dio la vuelta y tomó el camino de Seír.
es.R: Ese mismo día, Esaú se fue y regresó a Seír.

fr.L: Et Ésaü s’en retourna ce jour-là par son chemin vers Séir.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, Ésaü fit demi-tour et reprit la route de Séir.
fr.R: Ésaü est parti le jour même et il est retourné à Séir.

sw.L: Basi Esau akarudi siku ile njia yake kwenda Seiri.
sw.B: Siku ile ile Esau aligeuka, akashika njia ya kwenda Seiri.
sw.R: Esau aliondoka siku ile ile, akarudi Seiri.

source.text: וְיַעֲקֹב֙ נָסַ֣ע סֻכֹּ֔תָה וַיִּ֥בֶן ל֖וֹ בָּ֑יִת וּלְמִקְנֵ֨הוּ֙ עָשָׂ֣ה סֻכֹּ֔ת עַל־כֵּ֛ן קָרָ֥א שֵׁם־הַמָּק֖וֹם סֻכּֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Jacob set out to Succoth, and built for himself a house, and for his livestock he made booths; therefore he called the name of the place Succoth.

en.L: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth and built himself a house, and made booths for his livestock; that is why the name of the place is called Succoth.
en.B: Jacob for his part journeyed on to Succoth. He built a house to live in there and put up booths for his herds, and so the place got the name Succoth.
en.R: But Jacob traveled to Succoth. There he built a house for himself and shelters for his animals. So people named the place Succoth, which means "shelters".

es.L: Y Jacob partió a Sucot, y se edificó una casa, e hizo cabañas para su ganado; por eso se llama el nombre del lugar Sucot.
es.B: Jacob, por su parte, siguió hasta Sucot. Allí se construyó una casa para vivir y levantó enramadas para sus animales; por eso el lugar recibió el nombre de Sucot.
es.R: Pero Jacob viajó a Sucot. Allí se construyó una casa y unos refugios para sus animales. Por eso la gente llamó a ese lugar Sucot, que significa «refugios».

fr.L: Et Jacob partit pour Souccoth, et il se bâtit une maison, et il fit des cabanes pour son bétail ; c’est pourquoi on appelle le nom du lieu Souccoth.
fr.B: Jacob, lui, se rendit à Souccoth. Il s’y bâtit une maison et dressa des cabanes pour ses troupeaux ; c’est ainsi que ce lieu reçut le nom de Souccoth.
fr.R: Mais Jacob est allé à Souccoth. Là, il s’est construit une maison et il a fait des abris pour ses animaux. C’est pour cela qu’on a appelé cet endroit Souccoth, ce qui veut dire « abris ».

sw.L: Naye Yakobo alisafiri mpaka Sukothi, akajijengea nyumba, akaifanyia mifugo yake vibanda; ndiyo sababu jina la mahali pale linaitwa Sukothi.
sw.B: Yakobo yeye alisafiri hadi Sukothi. Akajijengea nyumba ya kukaa, akawajengea wanyama wake vibanda; kwa hiyo mahali pale pakaitwa Sukothi.
sw.R: Lakini Yakobo alisafiri kwenda Sukothi. Huko alijijengea nyumba, akawajengea wanyama wake mabanda. Kwa hiyo watu wakapaita mahali pale Sukothi, maana yake "mabanda."

decisions.choice: booths, Succoth: the place is named after the shelters
decisions.reason: Sukkot means "booths" or "shelters", simple huts of branches; later the Festival of Booths took the same name (Leviticus 23:42-43). Succoth lay east of the Jordan, near where the Jabbok meets it (Joshua 13:27).

decisions.choice: built himself a house: Jacob settles for a time
decisions.reason: A house, rather than a tent, suggests a stay of some length, though the text does not say how long.

decisions.choice: which means "shelters"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, which the Hebrew reader would hear at once.

source.text: וַיָּבֹא֩ יַעֲקֹ֨ב שָׁלֵ֜ם עִ֣יר שְׁכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בְּבֹא֖וֹ מִפַּדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם וַיִּ֖חַן אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Jacob safely [to the] city of Shechem which [is] in [the] land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-aram; and he camped before the city.

en.L: And Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem, which [is] in the land of Canaan, on his way from Paddan-aram, and he camped in front of the city.
en.B: Jacob arrived safe and sound at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, on his return from Paddan-aram, and he set up camp just outside the city.
en.R: On his way back from Paddan-aram, Jacob reached the city of Shechem in Canaan without harm. He camped near the city.

es.L: Y llegó Jacob sano y salvo a la ciudad de Siquem, que [está] en la tierra de Canaán, cuando venía de Padán Aram, y acampó frente a la ciudad.
es.B: Jacob llegó sano y salvo a la ciudad de Siquem, en la tierra de Canaán, a su regreso de Padán Aram, y montó su campamento a las afueras de la ciudad.
es.R: Al volver de Padán Aram, Jacob llegó sin ningún daño a la ciudad de Siquem, en Canaán. Acampó cerca de la ciudad.

fr.L: Et Jacob arriva sain et sauf à la ville de Sichem, qui [est] au pays de Canaan, à son retour de Paddân-Aram, et il campa devant la ville.
fr.B: Jacob arriva sain et sauf à la ville de Sichem, au pays de Canaan, à son retour de Paddân-Aram, et il installa son camp juste à l’extérieur de la ville.
fr.R: En revenant de Paddân-Aram, Jacob est arrivé sans aucun mal à la ville de Sichem, en Canaan. Il a campé près de la ville.

sw.L: Yakobo akafika salama katika mji wa Shekemu, ulio katika nchi ya Kanaani, alipokuja kutoka Padan-aramu, akapiga kambi mbele ya mji.
sw.B: Yakobo alifika salama salimini katika mji wa Shekemu katika nchi ya Kanaani, aliporudi kutoka Padan-aramu, akapiga kambi nje kidogo ya mji.
sw.R: Yakobo alipokuwa akirudi kutoka Padan-aramu, alifika katika mji wa Shekemu, huko Kanaani, bila kupata madhara. Akapiga kambi karibu na mji.

decisions.choice: safely: shalem, whole and unharmed
alternatives: to Shalem, a city of Shechem
decisions.reason: Shalem means whole, safe, at peace. Some ancient translations read it as a place name, "to Shalem". Read as "safely", it shows God keeping the promise of 28:15, 21: Jacob had vowed to serve God if he came back "in peace" (beshalom) to his father's house.

decisions.choice: Shechem: the place of Abraham's first altar in Canaan
decisions.reason: Abraham's first stop in the land was at Shechem, where God first promised him the land and he built an altar (12:6-7). Jacob enters the land at the same place.

source.text: וַיִּ֜קֶן אֶת־חֶלְקַ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽטָה־שָׁם֙ אָהֳל֔וֹ מִיַּ֥ד בְּנֵֽי־חֲמ֖וֹר אֲבִ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם בְּמֵאָ֖ה קְשִׂיטָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he bought the portion of the field where he had pitched there his tent, from [the] hand of [the] sons of Hamor, [the] father of Shechem, for a hundred qesitahs.

en.L: And he bought the plot of the field where he had pitched his tent from the hand of the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred qesitahs.
en.B: He bought the piece of ground where he had pitched his tent from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, paying a hundred pieces of silver.
en.R: Jacob bought the land where he had set up his tent. He paid a hundred pieces of silver to the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem.

es.L: Y compró la parcela del campo donde había plantado su tienda, de mano de los hijos de Hamor, padre de Siquem, por cien qesitas.
es.B: Compró a los hijos de Hamor, padre de Siquem, el terreno donde había plantado su tienda, por cien monedas de plata.
es.R: Jacob compró el terreno donde había puesto su tienda. Les pagó cien monedas de plata a los hijos de Hamor, el padre de Siquem.

fr.L: Et il acheta la parcelle de champ où il avait dressé sa tente, de la main des fils de Hamor, père de Sichem, pour cent qesitas.
fr.B: Il acheta aux fils de Hamor, père de Sichem, le terrain où il avait planté sa tente, pour cent pièces d’argent.
fr.R: Jacob a acheté le terrain où il avait installé sa tente. Il a payé cent pièces d’argent aux fils de Hamor, le père de Sichem.

sw.L: Akanunua sehemu ya shamba alipokuwa amepiga hema lake, kutoka mkononi mwa wana wa Hamori, baba yake Shekemu, kwa kesita mia moja.
sw.B: Alinunua kipande cha ardhi alipokuwa amepiga hema lake kutoka kwa wana wa Hamori, baba yake Shekemu, kwa vipande mia moja vya fedha.
sw.R: Yakobo alinunua ardhi alipokuwa amepiga hema lake. Aliwalipa wana wa Hamori, baba yake Shekemu, vipande mia moja vya fedha.

decisions.choice: qesitah: a unit of money of unknown value
decisions.reason: The qesitah appears only here, in Joshua 24:32 and in Job 42:11, and its weight or value is not known, so no modern equivalent can be given. The ancient Greek translation has "a hundred lambs".

decisions.choice: he bought the plot: the second piece of the promised land owned by the family
decisions.reason: Like Abraham at Machpelah (chapter 23), Jacob pays for land that God has promised to give. Joseph's bones were later buried in this field (Joshua 24:32; John 4:5).

decisions.choice: a hundred pieces of silver
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a general phrase for the unknown coin or weight; no units setting is used, because its value is not known. Literal keeps the Hebrew name.

source.text: וַיַּצֶּב־שָׁ֖ם מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּ֨קְרָא־ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ל אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he set up there an altar and called it El, God of Israel.

en.L: And he set up an altar there and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
en.B: He erected an altar there and gave it the name El-Elohe-Israel, "God is the God of Israel".
en.R: He built an altar there and named it El-Elohe-Israel. This means "God is the God of Israel."

es.L: Y erigió allí un altar y lo llamó El-Elohé-Israel.
es.B: Levantó allí un altar y le dio el nombre de El-Elohé-Israel, «Dios es el Dios de Israel».
es.R: Construyó allí un altar y le puso por nombre El-Elohé-Israel. Esto significa «Dios es el Dios de Israel».

fr.L: Et il dressa là un autel et l’appela El-Elohé-Israël.
fr.B: Il y éleva un autel et lui donna le nom d’El-Elohé-Israël, « Dieu est le Dieu d’Israël ».
fr.R: Il a construit un autel à cet endroit et l’a appelé El-Elohé-Israël. Cela veut dire « Dieu est le Dieu d’Israël ».

sw.L: Akasimamisha madhabahu pale, akaiita El-Elohe-Israeli.
sw.B: Alijenga madhabahu pale, akaipa jina El-Elohe-Israeli, "Mungu ni Mungu wa Israeli".
sw.R: Alijenga madhabahu pale, akaiita El-Elohe-Israeli. Maana yake ni "Mungu ni Mungu wa Israeli."

decisions.choice: El-Elohe-Israel: God, the God of Israel
alternatives: El is the God of Israel
the mighty one is the God of Israel
decisions.reason: The name joins the general word for God, El, to Jacob's new name, Israel (32:29). Jacob had vowed that if God brought him back safely, the LORD would be his God (28:21); now he names God as the God of Israel, that is, of himself. In time it becomes the name of God for the whole people.

decisions.choice: El-Elohe-Israel
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name as a name; Balanced and Readable add its meaning.
